steps.title: Declare the boundary: Required, optional and default input semantics

blocks.text: A default determines requiredness; a type that admits None determines nullability. These are different questions.
A nullable field with no default still requires presence. field: Type | None = None allows both omission and explicit null.
Send absence, explicit JSON null and a concrete value as separate requests. Compare each with the declared default and nullable type.

result_of.sql:
WITH inputs(ordinal, supplied, note) AS (VALUES (1,FALSE,NULL),(2,TRUE,NULL),(3,TRUE,'Leave at reception')), declarations(label, has_default) AS (VALUES ('note: str | None', FALSE), ('note: str | None = None', TRUE))
SELECT CASE WHEN NOT supplied THEN 'omitted' WHEN note IS NULL THEN 'explicit null' ELSE 'concrete string' END AS input,
 label AS declaration, (supplied OR has_default) AS accepted,
 CASE WHEN supplied OR has_default THEN note ELSE NULL END AS resulting_note
FROM orders CROSS JOIN inputs CROSS JOIN declarations ORDER BY ordinal, has_default

blocks.caption: Declaration comparison derived from the presence rule and supplied request bodies, not an HTTP run. Read resulting_note only where accepted is true.

blocks.text: Keep two columns in your mental model: must the field appear, and may its value be null? note: str | None requires presence but admits null. Adding = None allows omission too. Test missing, null and a concrete string separately against those declarations; “optional” alone does not identify both rules.

Start with the supplied nullable note declaration, then add its default. Send each supplied body separately before and after the change. Without a default, the field must appear even though null is allowed; with = None, omission is also allowed. Compare the declared presence rule with the admitted values instead of collapsing all three requests into one optional case.

public.prompt: Write test_required_note for app (note: str | None without a default) and test_default_note for default_app (note: str | None = None). For each, send three separate POST /orders/note requests with {}, {'note': None}, and {'note': 'Leave at reception'}. Assert omitted input returns 422 for app but 200 and {'note': None} for default_app; both declarations accept null and the string with 200 and the corresponding JSON payload. Preserve the supplied declarations. The threadless TestClient adapter uses the actual ASGI app.

files.content:
import asyncio, inspect, json, ast
import httpx
from contextlib import contextmanager

def _drive(coro):
    try:
        pending = coro.send(None)
    except StopIteration as done:
        return done.value
    raise RuntimeError('Harness encountered a suspending operation: ' + repr(pending))

async def _requests(application, requests):
    async with application.router.lifespan_context(application):
        async with httpx.AsyncClient(transport=httpx.ASGITransport(app=application, raise_app_exceptions=False), base_url='http://testserver') as client:
            out=[]
            for method,path,kwargs in requests:
                response=await client.request(method,path,**kwargs)
                try: body=response.json()
                except ValueError: body=response.text
                out.append({'status':response.status_code,'body':body})
            return out
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
class _InlineTransport(httpx.BaseTransport):
    def __init__(self,application):self.application=application
    def handle_request(self,request):
        response=_drive(self._handle(request))
        return httpx.Response(response.status_code,headers=response.headers,content=response.content,request=request)
    async def _handle(self,request):
        transport=httpx.ASGITransport(app=self.application)
        async with httpx.AsyncClient(transport=transport) as c:
            return await c.send(request)
def _client_init(self,application,**kwargs):
    self.app=application
    httpx.Client.__init__(self,transport=_InlineTransport(application),base_url='http://testserver',follow_redirects=True)
def _client_enter(self):
    self._lifespan=self.app.router.lifespan_context(self.app)
    _drive(self._lifespan.__aenter__())
    return self
def _client_exit(self,*exc):
    _drive(self._lifespan.__aexit__(*exc));self.close()
TestClient.__init__=_client_init
TestClient.__enter__=_client_enter
TestClient.__exit__=_client_exit
from pydantic import BaseModel
from fastapi import FastAPI
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
class NoteInput(BaseModel):
    note: str | None
app = FastAPI()
@app.post('/orders/note')
def set_note(body: NoteInput):
    return {'note': body.note}
class DefaultNoteInput(BaseModel):
    note: str | None = None
default_app = FastAPI()
@default_app.post('/orders/note')
def default_note(body: DefaultNoteInput): return {'note':body.note}
# TODO: write test_required_note and test_default_note, each with separate
# omitted, null and concrete-value requests and status/payload assertions.
def _case(which):
    test = test_required_note if which=='required' else test_default_note
    assert sum(isinstance(n,ast.Assert) for n in ast.walk(ast.parse(inspect.getsource(test))))>=5
    test()
    application=app if which=='required' else default_app
    return _drive(_requests(application,[('POST','/orders/note',{'json':j}) for j in ({},{'note':None},{'note':'Leave at reception'})]))
import inspect
from fastapi import FastAPI, Body
verification_app=FastAPI()

async def verify_case(payload: dict=Body(...)):
    result=_case(payload['case'])
    if inspect.isawaitable(result):return await result
    return result
verify_case = verification_app.post('/_verify')(verify_case)

steps.title: Declare the boundary: FastAPI OpenAPI generation from typed route contracts

blocks.text: FastAPI normally serves the generated OpenAPI document at /openapi.json. It describes operations and data schemas.
Typed body declarations contribute input schemas; response models contribute output schemas to the generated public contract.
Locate the endpoint’s method entry under paths, then follow its schema references into components to find the public input and output definitions.

annotations.text: POST /orders: requestBody reference → components.schemas.OrderInput; response reference → OrderOutput. quantity is input, id is output.

blocks.text: Navigate by endpoint path and method first. Follow the body and response references into components, then compare their field definitions with the typed declarations. OpenAPI is generated from those declarations; it describes operations and schemas. Reading the document does not establish every runtime outcome, and schema details need not be inline in the operation entry.

In the supplied POST /orders excerpt, follow the request-body reference to OrderInput and the response reference to OrderOutput. The input definition has quantity; the output definition has id. These are different public definitions contributed by the body and response-model declarations. Retrieve the generated document at /openapi.json and navigate through paths and components rather than assuming every field is inline. This is contract structure, not proof of every runtime result.
